appraisal_events.evidence: il était ravi que je donnasse de ces dîners extras... « J'ai pour principe que, comme on dit vulgairement, on ne doit pas estamper le client. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Aimé is portrayed as an attentive, principled maître d'hôtel who takes evident pleasure in serving the narrator well and explicitly protects him from being overcharged.

appraisal_events.evidence: il l'avait fait avec une majesté sacerdotale... le sacrificateur... cette prosectomie donna-t-elle, comme la naissance du Christ ou l'Hégire, le point de départ d'un calendrier différent
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator mock-heroically elevates the director's turkey-carving into a quasi-sacred, epoch-making feat, gently ironizing his self-importance while the watching waiters genuinely admire him.

appraisal_events.evidence: je savais que Legrandin, lequel se faisait maintenant appeler Legrand de Méséglise, n'y avait aucune espèce de droit
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator flatly states that Legrandin's newly adopted, more distinguished-sounding surname has no legitimate basis, exposing his social pretension.

status_effects.explanation: Aimé's diligence and honesty toward the narrator as a favored client cast him in a positive light.
Within the staged scene he gains stature among his staff, though the narrator's mock-heroic framing keeps the elevation comically undercut.
His adopted aristocratic-sounding name is exposed as baseless, diminishing his social pretensions.

ambiguities: The reference to duc de Guermantes ('cérémonieusement méprisant') is only a comparative aside used to characterize Chevregny's contrasting speech style, not a staged event about the duc himself, so he was omitted.
'Swann Crécy' refers to an unrelated American who married into the Guermantes family, not to Charles Swann; this apparent name match was not scored as the character Swann.

The director's turkey-carving episode is narrated with comic, mock-heroic irony, making the net valence (genuine elevation vs. gentle mockery of vanity) inherently unstable; scored conservatively as mixed.
